title.en: Chronicle of Gaozu's Meritorious Officials and Marquises

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：古者人臣功有五品，以德立宗廟定社稷曰勳，以言曰勞，用力曰功，明其等曰伐，積日曰閱。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: In ancient times, a minister's service was classified in five grades: establishing the ancestral temples and securing the altars of soil and grain through virtue was called xun; service through counsel was called lao; service through physical exertion was called gong; making clear one's rank was called fa; and accumulated days of service was called yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: In ancient times, a minister's service was classified in five grades: establishing the ancestral temples and securing the realm through virtue was called xun; service through counsel was called lao; service through physical exertion was called gong; making clear one's rank was called fa; and accumulated days of service was called yue.

sentences.zh: 封爵之誓曰：「使河如帶，泰山若厲。

translations.literal: The oath sworn at enfeoffment said: 'May the Yellow River become narrow as a belt, and Mount Tai wear down to a whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: The oath sworn when titles were granted said: 'May the Yellow River become narrow as a belt, and Mount Tai wear down to a whetstone.

sentences.zh: 國以永寧，爰及苗裔。」

translations.literal: May the state endure in peace, reaching even to descendants and posterity.'
translations.idiomatic: May the state enjoy lasting peace, extending down to its descendants and posterity."

sentences.zh: 始未嘗不欲固其根本，而枝葉稍陵夷衰微也。

translations.literal: At first they never failed to wish to strengthen the root, yet gradually the branches and leaves declined and weakened.
translations.idiomatic: At first, they never failed to wish to strengthen their foundations, yet gradually the branches and leaves declined and weakened.

sentences.zh: 余讀高祖侯功臣，察其首封，所以失之者，曰：異哉新聞！

translations.literal: I have read about the marquises among Gaozu's meritorious officials, examined the time of their initial enfeoffment, and considered why they lost their titles. I said: How extraordinary—such tidings!
translations.idiomatic: I have read about the marquises created from Gaozu's meritorious officials, examined when they were first enfeoffed, and considered the reasons their titles were lost. I said: how strange these recent accounts are!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰「協和萬國」，遷于夏商，或數千歲。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says, "Harmonize the myriad states." From Xia through Shang, some endured for several thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Bring the myriad states into harmony." From Xia through Shang, some endured for several thousand years.

sentences.zh: 蓋周封八百，幽厲之後，見於春秋。

translations.literal: Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred, and after You and Li, they appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred nobles, and after the reigns of You and Li, they appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 尚書有唐虞之侯伯，歷三代千有餘載，自全以蕃衛天子，豈非篤於仁義，奉上法哉？

translations.literal: The Documents mention the marquises and earls of Tang and Yu, who endured through the Three Dynasties for more than a thousand years, preserving themselves to guard and protect the Son of Heaven—was this not steadfast devotion to benevolence and righteousness and loyalty to the laws above?
translations.idiomatic: The Documents speak of the marquises and earls of Tang and Yu, who passed through the Three Dynasties for more than a thousand years, preserving themselves while guarding and shielding the Son of Heaven. Was this not because they were deeply committed to benevolence and righteousness and upheld the laws from above?

sentences.zh: 漢興，功臣受封者百有餘人。

translations.literal: When Han arose, over a hundred meritorious officials received enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose, more than a hundred meritorious officials were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 天下初定，故大城名都散亡，戶口可得而數者十二三，是以大侯不過萬家，小者五六百戶。

translations.literal: The realm had just been pacified, so great cities and famous capitals lay scattered and lost. The households that could be counted were only one or two in ten; therefore the largest marquisates did not exceed ten thousand families, while the smallest had five or six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm had only just been pacified, great cities and famous capitals lay dispersed and ruined. Only two or three households in ten could be counted, and so the largest marquisates had no more than ten thousand families, while the smaller ones held five or six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後數世，民咸歸鄉里，戶益息，蕭、曹、絳、灌之屬或至四萬，小侯自倍，富厚如之。

translations.literal: After several generations, the people all returned to their native places, households increased, and the likes of Xiao, Cao, Jiang, Guan sometimes reached forty thousand, small marquises doubled, becoming wealthy like them.
translations.idiomatic: After several generations, the people all returned to their native villages, households increased, and figures like Xiao, Cao, Jiang, and Guan sometimes reached forty thousand households. Small marquises doubled their holdings, becoming wealthy like them.

sentences.zh: 子孫驕溢，忘其先，淫嬖。

translations.literal: Their descendants became arrogant and extravagant, forgetting their ancestors, indulging in debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants became arrogant and extravagant, forgetting their ancestors and indulging in debauchery.

sentences.zh: 至太初百年之閒，見侯五，餘皆坐法隕命亡國，秏矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Taichu, within a century, only five marquises remain visible, the rest all perished through law violations, losing their lives and states, gone.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taichu period, within a century, only five marquises remain visible; the rest all perished through violations of law, losing their lives and states—utterly gone.

sentences.zh: 罔亦少密焉，然皆身無兢兢於當世之禁云。

translations.literal: Perhaps the net was cast less tightly, yet none maintained careful reverence toward the prohibitions of their own age.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the legal net was somewhat less tightly drawn, yet none of them maintained anxious reverence toward the prohibitions of their own time.

sentences.zh: 居今之世，志古之道，所以自鏡也，未必盡同。

translations.literal: Living in the present age, observing the ways of antiquity, one may use them as a mirror, but they are not necessarily all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Living in the present age and observing the ways of antiquity provides a mirror for self-reflection, but they are not necessarily identical.

sentences.zh: 帝王者各殊禮而異務，要以成功為統紀，豈可緄乎？

translations.literal: Emperors and kings each had different rites and different priorities, but ultimately success was the standard by which they were judged—how could one bind them to a single pattern?
translations.idiomatic: Emperors and kings differed in rites and varied in priorities; in the end, success was the thread by which they were judged. How could they be bound to a single pattern?

sentences.zh: 觀所以得尊寵及所以廢辱，亦當世得失之林也，何必舊聞？

translations.literal: Observing what brought honor and favor and what brought disgrace and humiliation is also a record of the gains and losses of the age—why must one rely on old accounts?
translations.idiomatic: Observing what brought honor and favor, and what brought disgrace and humiliation, is also a record of the gains and losses of the age—why must one rely on old accounts?

sentences.zh: 於是謹其終始，表其文，頗有所不盡本末；

translations.literal: Therefore, I have carefully examined their beginnings and ends and set out their records in a table, though in some cases the roots and branches are not fully complete;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, I have carefully traced their beginnings and ends and presented their records in a table, though in some cases the full roots and branches cannot be recovered;

sentences.zh: 著其明，疑者闕之。

translations.literal: Recorded what was clear, left doubtful matters blank.
translations.idiomatic: I recorded what was clear, and left doubtful matters blank.

sentences.zh: 後有君子，欲推而列之，得以覽焉。

translations.literal: If later gentlemen wish to investigate and list them, they may peruse this.
translations.idiomatic: If future gentlemen wish to investigate and arrange them, they may peruse this work.
